claims.text: Tencent Tech published a lightly edited transcript of what it describes as a roughly three-hour-forty-four-minute closed-door investor meeting with Liang Wenfeng, sourced from a recording pointing to a May 20, 2026 meeting date.

The transcript, as published, has the speaker saying Huawei allocates DeepSeek roughly 16,000 cards of capacity, that four Huawei cards equal one Nvidia card, and that broader ecosystem parity should arrive within a year.
Moonshot's own API pricing for Kimi K3 is $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, versus $0.95 and $4 for predecessor Kimi K2.6.
On Artificial Analysis's own AA-Omniscience benchmark, K3's accuracy climbed from 33% to 46% relative to K2.6 — but its hallucination rate climbed alongside it, from 39% to 51%.
The full open weights are scheduled for HuggingFace on July 27 under a Modified MIT license.
On the broader Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.1, K3 scored 57.1 against GPT-5.6 Sol Max's 58.9 and Claude Fable 5's 59.9.
OSTP Director Michael Kratsios posted on X that Moonshot AI distilled Anthropic's Fable and acquired GB300-equipped servers with access to GB300s in Thailand.
Treasury's parallel review, per multiple outlets, now reportedly spans four labs rather than one: Moonshot, DeepSeek, MiniMax, and Alibaba.
Moonshot's Huang Zhenxin named three architecture changes — Moon Clip, Kimi Delta Attention, and Attention Residuals — as the actual source of K3's gains.
Braden Hancock and Nathan Lambert argued the roughly two-week gap between Fable 5's release and K3's launch left too little time for large-scale distillation to explain K3's gains.
Chinese embassy spokesperson Liu Chang called the allegations entirely unfounded / pure slander; Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said China opposes politicizing tech issues.
Jensen Huang told Axios These Chinese models are excellent, that American firms should absolutely be free to use them, and that there is zero possibility China displaces U.S. AI labs.
On July 24, 2026, a 25-company coalition published Open Weights and American AI Leadership; OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google did not sign.
Jensen Huang publicized the letter in the first post of his career on X.
No signatory roster for the Little Tech Association's nearly 200 companies has been published.
White House spokesperson Liz Huston offered a generic talking point and an unnamed official dismissed ban-imminent speculation as baseless.
ByteDance committed $5.6 billion to Ascend 950PR orders, implying roughly 350,000 units.
The PHLX Semiconductor Index fell approximately 10% in the week of Kimi K3's launch; global semiconductor stocks had shed roughly $3.3 trillion since a June 22 peak.
MOFCOM is reportedly weighing a tiered export-control regime for AI model weights, tied to the unwound Meta-Manus acquisition.
The U.S. and China plan to hold their first official AI dialogue in September 2026, ahead of a planned September 24 Xi Jinping visit, with Bessent leading the U.S. delegation.
H.R. 4142 remains referred to committee with no recorded markup; Senate companion S.2177 is similarly parked in committee.
Sam Altman said on X he was glad to see the letter and wants the US to win in AI both in open source and proprietary models.
DeepSeek is reportedly in early discussions for a second funding round at a pre-money valuation near $71 billion.

Anthropic reported in February 2026 that it had identified industrial-scale attempts by three labs, including Moonshot, to extract Claude's capabilities via roughly 16 million exchanges through some 24,000 accounts; Fable 5 did not launch until June 9, 2026.
